advisory_items.category: evidence-quality / blind spot (carried from T5R-03, NOT escalated)
advisory_items.finding: scratch/verify_replay.py:restore_modes() still force-chmods the fresh-delivery copy to 0644 and back to the manifest value before that leg's manifest check (observed mode_reset_and_restore_count=45), so the fresh leg cannot detect mode drift. I deliberately do NOT escalate this to blocking: the mode fix did not change the function's semantics; the current-tree leg is not blind (verify_manifest compares delivered modes directly - that leg is what surfaced T5R-03's defect); and no delivered claim is false, since the reset is disclosed in the same JSON via mode_reset_and_restore_count.
advisory_items.suggested_fix: Remove restore_modes() so the copytree result is checked as-is, or record the pre-rewrite mismatch rather than erasing it.

advisory_items.category: portability / bookkeeping (carried from T5R-03, NOT escalated; quantified this round)
advisory_items.finding: The manifest records umask-coupled modes: 29 entries at 100664, 11 at 100644, 5 at 100755. My scratch simulation on identical delivered bytes shows that fresh file creation under umask 022 yields 34/45 raw-mode mismatches (29 from the 100664 group plus 5 execute-bit losses) and under umask 002 yields 16/45 (11 plus 5). Normalizing to git semantics (execute bit only) removes the pure-umask component entirely. The mixed 100644/100664 recording of same-role data files is itself evidence that the recorded mode is the author's umask rendering rather than a normalized intent. Not blocking: the delivered state does match the manifest strictly in this environment; the risk is confined to environments or copy paths without mode preservation (cp without -p, tar without -p).
advisory_items.suggested_fix: Record only the git-normalized mode (100644/100755), or normalize file modes before hashing.

advisory_items.category: error-surface contract (carried from T5R-03, NOT escalated)
advisory_items.finding: caller_validator.py raises bare SystemExit for a --runtime-root inside the delivered run tree, and verify_replay.py does the same for an in-tree or pre-existing --work-root. Both emit no JSON result object, so a caller falls back to MALFORMED_RESULT/FC_INTERNAL rather than a canonical FC_ARBITRARY_PATH. Fail-closed and writes nothing, but off the declared error surface. Unchanged by the mode fix.
advisory_items.suggested_fix: Emit the normal rejected JSON envelope with a canonical fail_closed_code for these guard rails.

justification: The T5R-03 blocking item was narrow - a delivery-layer mode conformance failure, not a content defect - and the closer's fix is the stronger of the two remedies T5R-03 offered. By restoring the execute bits on the four scripts rather than editing the manifest or re-emitting evidence, 115f396 made every pre-existing 45/45 assertion true while changing zero bytes, so the six evidence surfaces remain exactly the author's original record and are now reproducible. I proved this independently: 45/45 bytes and SHA-256, 45/45 modes, 45/45 three-way blob identity, the four scripts and watcher.sh at 100755 in the worktree, the .git/index and the HEAD tree, the other 41 entries with zero drift, and a direct object-store comparison showing the run tree changed only at 115f396 with zero blob content differences and exactly the four expected mode flips. The headline delivery claims now all reproduce from delivered bytes: the no-prerequisite entry point returns rc=0 with four rounds of 23/23 and identical normalized outcomes that I recomputed from the raw records rather than trusting the summary, both trees passing manifest checks with empty failure and extra sets, and my own before/after scan of sha256, bytes, mode and mtime_ns across all 46 files (gitignore view included) proving zero writes and no residue after every run I performed. Regressions are intact - watcher execute bit in three layers, X06A/X06B/Z01 and the full 23-case matrix exact, G1 5/5, usage self-consistency with execution_chat_usage honestly left UNRESOLVED, four-class separation with overall_pass_field_forbidden, 7/7 frozen protections with FP-RAW-RECORD-INTEGRITY untouched by 0 content differences, TASK_PROMPT byte-identical to its dispatch source, and embedded pins plus three target git_blob_ids all exact. The closer's disclosure is accurate on every point, including the delicate one: T5R-03's receipt records a direct import of caller_validator while its side-effect statement claims zero writes in the reviewed run or repository, so the leftover __pycache__ was indeed undisclosed, and it is now gone. I reviewed all four carried advisories specifically for escalation and kept each at advisory: the mode fix does not make any delivered claim false, ADVISORY-1's blind spot is confined to the fresh-copy leg while the current-tree leg remains the effective detector, and ADVISORY-2 is a cross-environment portability property that I quantified rather than merely restated. Because there are zero blocking items and every headline claim is independently reproducible from the delivered state by the standard T5R-01, T5R-02 and T5R-03 applied consistently, ACCEPTED is the consistent verdict.
